title: Noisy-tenant ingest circuit-breaker with schema-migration safe-fallback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Add a tenant-aware circuit-breaker to the structured log ingestion path that detects high-rate noisy tenants and applies graduated protective measures while preserving safe schema-migration behavior for downstream consumers.

Background: We have recurring incidents where a small number of tenants emit malformed or extremely high-volume structured logs after a schema rollout, causing high CPU and write amplification in the Loki ingestion cluster and increasing latency for all tenants. Current mitigations are manual (tenant throttling, sidecar restarts) and risk data loss during schema transitions. We need an automated, observable, and reversible mechanism that: identifies noisy behavior, applies rate-limited backpressure and sample-and-queue fallback, and automatically falls back to a schema-safe forwarding mode when clients are on incompatible schema versions.

Scope: Implement a middleware stage in the ingress pipeline (pre-parse step) that: 1) maintains per-tenant rolling rate estimates (events/sec, bytes/sec, error-rate), 2) flags tenants that exceed adaptive thresholds for noisy/malformed traffic, 3) applies graduated reactions: warning, soft-drop (sample 1/N), hard-drop (reject with clear error code), and schema-safe forward (strip optional fields and forward to a compatibility topic). Also add admin controls (tenant opt-out, dry-run, manual overrides) and automated health signals to the Console.

Design notes:
- Thresholds are workload-aware: combine absolute rate with relative deviation from tenant baseline.
- Schema-safe forward mode relies on a lightweight transform layer that strips unknown fields and coerces types according to our canonical ingest schema; this ensures downstream parsers don't fail during migrations.
- Circuit-breaker state machine must be persisted in the key-value store (etcd) with TTL-backed automatic decay to avoid permanent blackholes.
- Should emit structured audit events for state transitions so Security and SRE can trace actions.
- Prioritize cheap, predictable checks in the fast path; heavy validation should run asynchronously in parallel to avoid adding latency to accepted events.

Rollout plan: Canary in a single region for non-critical tenants (dry-run mode), evaluate signal SLOs for 72h, enable soft-drop for top offenders, then enable schema-safe forward where migrations have been detected. Provide a rollback knob to remove circuit-breaker rules instantly via API.

Acceptance criteria are below.
acceptance_criteria: New middleware stage deployed behind feature flag and running in dry-run mode (no traffic dropped) in eu-west-1.
Per-tenant rate and error metrics emitted (metrics: ingest.tenant.events_per_sec, ingest.tenant.bytes_per_sec, ingest.tenant.malformed_pct).
State transitions emitted as structured audit events (event.ingest.circuitbreaker.{tenant,old_state,new_state,reason}).
Soft-drop and hard-drop behaviors respect opt-out and manual override flags and are reversible via API and Console toggle.
Schema-safe forward mode transforms at least three incompatible message patterns in test harness without downstream parser failures.
End-to-end test coverage for the state machine and key failure scenarios added to telemetry-integration CI.
Monitoring dashboard in Console showing per-tenant noisy tenants, impact on write latency, and number of events forwarded to compatibility topic.

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive sampling reduces cluster load but may hide customer data needed for debugging. We will default to soft-drop + schema-safe forward and reserve hard-drop for confirmed noisy tenants.
We deliberately keep the heavy schema validation async to avoid adding tail latency to the fast path. This means we may accept some malformed payloads which are later quarantined for reprocessing.
Leader failover: state sync implemented via TTL-backed keys and leader-epoch token to prevent split-brain. Still need failure-mode tests.
